target.name: Harbinger
target.founder: John Harris, Phillip Weicker, Will Eberts

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $100M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Harbinger is a Series C-stage transportation company that has raised $358M to date. The comparable universe consists of 7 private frontier-transportation firms including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, and ZeroAvia; no public transportation peers were identified with sufficient comparability at this stage and valuation tier.

The stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach. Using $100M as a proxy for total capital raised to date and applying a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C progression, this method implies a valuation of $170M. A peer-median approach was not viable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables in transportation—only 3 peers exist in the sector, but none satisfied the filters for narrow-set reliability (minimum 3 datapoints required), making a broader cross-sector median unreliable.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $144M (low) to $195M (high), with a median of $170M. This range reflects a ±15% band around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the absence of granular comparable data at Harbinger's exact stage and valuation tier, and reliance on a single methodological input rather than multiple convergent approaches. The valuation is most sensitive to refinement of the stage-step multiplier and capital-raise trajectory relative to the private transportation peer set.
